$$
\{\begin{aligned}2k-6=0 \\ 3k-9=0 \\ -6k+18=0\end{aligned}
$$

and for each of these equations, we obtain $k=3.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119625 :question/worked-solution "We need to solve the equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -3 & 6 \\ 4 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is ${x}_{1}$, and we have one free variable, ${x}_{2}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ in terms of ${x}_{2}.$

From the first equation we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2},$ so the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2}\in R\}.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186417735 :answer-field/correct "answer-78246ec8-609c-551f-b0ac-0dadda339bf8" :answer-field/choices ["answer-a3181278-1876-5206-9569-f7c580389091" "answer-78246ec8-609c-551f-b0ac-0dadda339bf8" "answer-1dea2883-7aed-50ab-88db-338d6b05d1d2" "answer-6d08ac3a-bf71-57e5-86bb-45513f396dce" "answer-bcdbf8dd-4179-511e-ac05-173b55d1fa27"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a3181278-1876-5206-9569-f7c580389091" :answer/id #uuid "a3181278-1876-5206-9569-f7c580389091" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2}\in R\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-78246ec8-609c-551f-b0ac-0dadda339bf8" :answer/id #uuid "78246ec8-609c-551f-b0ac-0dadda339bf8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2}\in R\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1dea2883-7aed-50ab-88db-338d6b05d1d2" :answer/id #uuid "1dea2883-7aed-50ab-88db-338d6b05d1d2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{[\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2}\in R\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6d08ac3a-bf71-57e5-86bb-45513f396dce" :answer/id #uuid "6d08ac3a-bf71-57e5-86bb-45513f396dce" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{[\begin{aligned}6{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2}\in R\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bcdbf8dd-4179-511e-ac05-173b55d1fa27" :answer/id #uuid "bcdbf8dd-4179-511e-ac05-173b55d1fa27" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{1}\in R\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186317454 :question/worked-solution "We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

The second equation tells us that ${x}_{2}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{1}+2(0)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=0.
$$

So, we conclude that $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ is the only solution to this system.

Therefore, $\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186316831 :answer-field/correct "answer-bd56a073-7763-5f3e-8627-e620cdb34e7b" :answer-field/choices ["answer-bd56a073-7763-5f3e-8627-e620cdb34e7b" "answer-9e92c0f2-12f6-52e4-bc39-5f630e281daf" "answer-6572e448-2a1b-54fa-b7eb-b164a363dfcd" "answer-b0b063f1-874e-516d-844c-6910584fd9fa" "answer-77ade1d1-f580-5223-b0a2-1bf51cbff285"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bd56a073-7763-5f3e-8627-e620cdb34e7b" :answer/id #uuid "bd56a073-7763-5f3e-8627-e620cdb34e7b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{0\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9e92c0f2-12f6-52e4-bc39-5f630e281daf" :answer/id #uuid "9e92c0f2-12f6-52e4-bc39-5f630e281daf" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2}\in R\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6572e448-2a1b-54fa-b7eb-b164a363dfcd" :answer/id #uuid "6572e448-2a1b-54fa-b7eb-b164a363dfcd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{1}\in R\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b0b063f1-874e-516d-844c-6910584fd9fa" :answer/id #uuid "b0b063f1-874e-516d-844c-6910584fd9fa" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{1}\in R\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-77ade1d1-f580-5223-b0a2-1bf51cbff285" :answer/id #uuid "77ade1d1-f580-5223-b0a2-1bf51cbff285" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2}\in R\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121063 :tutorial/content "Let's again consider the following matrix:

![](images/8f/8fa69630c71d5106ed04a5281681992687174891b1c0978521c12e914cb3a0b0.svg)

To find an expression for the null space using set-builder notation, we need to find all the solutions of $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.$ Let's start by considering the augmented matrix $[A\,|\, \mathbf{0}]$ and finding its reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,0] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st column). The second column is not a pivot column.

Now, we convert the reduced matrix back into a system, as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $\color{blue}x_1$ is a basic variable (it corresponds to the pivot column), while $\color{red}x_2$ is a free variable (it corresponds to the non-pivot column). Because there is a free variable, the system $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ has infinitely many solutions. 

From the first equation we get ${\color{blue}x_1}=-3{\color{red}x_2},$ so the set of all the solutions of $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ is
![](images/8c/8c5541adb07cb58136d71fb4e3218981f1717b929f22acbe55d133cd0c395870.svg)

**Note:** It is not necessary to consider the full augmented matrix $[A \,|\, \mathbf{0}]$ since the last column won't be changed during the process of reduction. Really, we just need to find the reduced row echelon form of the matrix $A$ and then set up the corresponding system." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]}]

:step/content {:db/id 17592186121063 :tutorial/content "Let's again consider the following matrix:

![](images/8f/8fa69630c71d5106ed04a5281681992687174891b1c0978521c12e914cb3a0b0.svg)

To find an expression for the null space using set-builder notation, we need to find all the solutions of $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.$ Let's start by considering the augmented matrix $[A\,|\, \mathbf{0}]$ and finding its reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,0] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st column). The second column is not a pivot column.

Now, we convert the reduced matrix back into a system, as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $\color{blue}x_1$ is a basic variable (it corresponds to the pivot column), while $\color{red}x_2$ is a free variable (it corresponds to the non-pivot column). Because there is a free variable, the system $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ has infinitely many solutions. 

From the first equation we get ${\color{blue}x_1}=-3{\color{red}x_2},$ so the set of all the solutions of $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ is

The linear algebra section covers crucial machine learning fundamentals such as matrices, vector spaces, diagonalization, projections, singular value decomposition, and regression, as well as dimensionality reduction techniques such as principal component analysis. Logical reasoning and Boolean functions are also studied, providing important conceptual motivation for understanding the expressive limitations of some simple machine learning models, such as why certain functions (e.g. XOR) cannot be represented by a single-layer neural network.
Students then explore matrices in-depth. They study Gaussian elimination, solve systems of equations, learn about determinants and their properties, and compute inverse matrices. These tools form the computational backbone of many machine learning algorithms.
As part of this course, students perform a deep dive into vector spaces, exploring linear independence, subspaces, bases, dimension, rank, and nullity. They also study operations such as the Hadamard product, which appears naturally in element-wise computations in neural networks. Students generalize key concepts to abstract vector spaces and inner product spaces, and study orthogonality, projections, and the Gram–Schmidt process.
Students will learn how to find eigenvectors of a matrix, compute matrix diagonalizations, and extend these ideas to orthogonal diagonalization of symmetric matrices. These techniques underpin dimensionality reduction methods and are central to understanding the structure of data.
The course then develops key applications of linear algebra in machine learning. Students study singular value decomposition and its relationship to principal component analysis, and learn how these tools are used for dimensionality reduction, feature extraction, and identifying structure in high-dimensional datasets. Linear least-squares problems and regression techniques are also studied as foundational methods for fitting models to data.
A solid grasp of multivariable calculus is essential for understanding modern machine learning algorithms. In this course, students become well-versed in partial derivatives and gradient vectors (used in gradient-based optimization), the multivariable chain rule (essential for backpropagation), and vector-valued functions. Students extend differentiation to maps between multi-dimensional vector spaces and develop the tools of vector and matrix calculus used to compute gradients of loss functions in neural networks.
Students also study optimization of multivariable functions, including critical points, second derivative tests, and constrained optimization using Lagrange multipliers. These techniques form the mathematical foundation of algorithms such as support vector machines and constrained optimization problems in machine learning.
Students work with standard multivariable surfaces to build intuition for loss surfaces, and study double integrals as a tool for understanding continuous probability distributions.
On the probability and statistics side, students study discrete and continuous random variables, including probability density functions, cumulative distribution functions, transformations, expectation, moments, variance, and Bayes' theorem. Important probability distributions are explored in detail.
Students extend their understanding to joint, marginal, and conditional distributions, as well as sums and products of random variables. Topics such as covariance, correlation, and multivariate normal distributions are introduced, which are essential in probabilistic modeling.
